title: Code gates catch broken items, not weak ones
statement: Hard-block in code only what code detects reliably, keep keyword and length counts advisory, and check quality and correctness separately, since a well-formed item can be weak or wrong.
example: A deterministic suite caught 19 of 102 failing items and rejected 22 of 351 passing ones.
detail: On 30 scored AP question sets, a stage validator passed 12 of the 14 failing sets and wrongly failed 1 of the 16 passing ones, and its results note concluded that hard gates are a safety layer, not a quality judge, since most failures were semantic rather than schema or leak failures. Its first version also hard-blocked reading-style, source-referential stems and over-blocked known passing items, so the split kept hard gates for schema, missing fields, answer leaks, extreme length and key clustering and made wording flags advisory. A separate probe of a deterministic suite on 461 generated items caught 19 of 102 failures and rejected 22 of 351 passes, and a shape-only acceptance test passed 25 of 25 in 0.006 s while a graded retest of the same service scored 8 of 20. Code gates catch broken items, not weak ones. Keyword and wording counts stay advisory, as does length unless it is extreme, since a valid shape does not show quality.
against: A later design hard-rejects on a semantic check before grading: "reject any item whose answer is derivable from the stimulus" (icloud-work/aptraining/workspace/comms/MCQSET_GENERATION_LEVER.md, line 16). The 8 of 20 retest used a thinner generic prompt than the graded specialist solvers (aptraining-local/den-of-ideation/from_den/2026-05-25T0758Z_BLOCKED_WORKFLOW_GENERIC_MCq_RETEST.md, line 18), so it shows what the shape check missed, not how good the specialists were. The validator figures come from a replay of archived outputs, not fresh generation (aptraining-local/den-of-ideation/experiments/b0035_mcqset_stage_validator/RESULTS.md, line 7). Used as gates rather than as scores, cheap word checks still catch real cues, such as the absolute words found in 35% of generated items in one review (`icloud-work/k_12_social_studies/python/docs/EVALUATION-RESULTS-2026-02-23.md`). A later run found: A Grade 3 course hard-blocks a modest length tell, failing the build when the key is more than 1.25 times as long as the longest wrong option or under 1/1.25 of the shortest, where this record keeps length counts advisory and blocks only extreme length. The same course's quality pass agrees that spread around the mean is not a defect, calling option lengths that span 44–91% of the mean a matter of style (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-6/distilled/04-CONTENT-AUTHORING.md`).

**What 12% means:** The model now generates MCQ_SET format (3 questions, stimulus, all required fields). But the quality threshold (factual_accuracy, stimulus_quality) was still failing 88% of the time.
**What 12% doesn't mean:** We solved MCQ_SET quality. We solved MCQ_SET FORMAT. These are different problems.

The limitation is critical: you can force the model to emit a syntactically valid JSON field for `"year": <int>`, but you cannot force the value to be `1919` rather than `1914` via grammar constraints alone. Semantic fact-checking requires a different mechanism.
